overview: Britain seeks a claim to Japan's former military copper stocks via its Tokyo mission; State opts for market sale over allocation, prioritizing SCAP's financial return and keeping SCAP informed of US copper prices.

people.name: H. C. Bugbee
people.role: U.S. official in London; sender of the airgram

people.name: Robert L. Hall
people.role: Official of the British Ministry of Supply

people.name: Roswell H. Whitman
people.role: Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs

people.name: W. S. McCormick
people.role: Official, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs

people.name: Arthur Gardiner
people.role: Official of the U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.title: Airgram from London on British interest in Japanese copper stocks
subfiles.about: Reports British plans to seek a share of copper and copper-alloy stocks available in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: London relays British plans to claim a share of Japan's military-origin copper and brass stocks through its Tokyo mission.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on copper stocks and disposal arrangements in Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses the reported Japanese copper stocks, potential surplus, United States demand, and alternative methods of sale.
subfiles.summary: McCormick reviews Japan's copper stocks from former military holdings, favoring market sale over an allocation formula.

subfiles.title: Letter to Arthur Gardiner on marketing Japanese copper
subfiles.about: Recommends that SCAP sell Japanese copper for the highest return instead of dividing it among purchasers through an allocation formula.
subfiles.summary: Whitman tells Gardiner State favors market sale of Japanese copper over allocation, asking him to track US copper prices.

interest: Shows 1946-47 British-American dispute over disposing of Japan's leftover military copper stocks.
